basic_information.name: Meilisearch
basic_information.creator: Meili SAS (Paris, France)
basic_information.description: Meilisearch is an open-source, Rust-based search engine that provides lightning-fast full-text, semantic, and hybrid search through a RESTful HTTP API. Originally designed as a typo-tolerant keyword search engine, it has evolved into a unified search and AI retrieval platform with native hybrid search combining its bucket-sorting keyword relevance engine with vector-based semantic search. Its key differentiators are sub-50ms response times out of the box, instant indexing, built-in typo tolerance, and developer-friendly setup requiring minimal configuration. Meilisearch is MIT-licensed, making it one of the most permissively licensed search engines available, and it positions itself as a developer-friendly, cost-effective alternative to Algolia and Elasticsearch for both traditional search and RAG pipelines.
basic_information.release_date: Initial release 2018; v1.0 stable February 2023; v1.13 stabilized AI-powered search (2025); v1.16 introduced multimodal embeddings (October 2025); latest updates include /chat endpoint and dynamic sharding (January 2026)
basic_information.github_stars: ~48,000-56,000 stars on GitHub (as of February 2026; sources vary between 50K-56K)

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Single-binary, disk-based architecture backed by LMDB (Lightning Memory-Mapped Database). Stores both the inverted index for keyword search and vector embeddings on disk via memory-mapped files, allowing indexes much larger than RAM. Originally single-node only, but v1.13+ introduced remote federated search as groundwork for sharding, and January 2026 updates enabled dynamic shard addition for horizontal scaling. Meilisearch Cloud Enterprise Edition supports sharding for distributed workloads. Available as self-hosted binary, Docker container, or fully managed Meilisearch Cloud.
technical_architecture.language: Rust (core engine); client SDKs in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, PHP, Ruby, Go, Java, C#, Swift, Dart, and Rust
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports arbitrary embedding dimensions. Common configurations: 1536 (OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 and text-embedding-3-small), 3072 (text-embedding-3-large), 768 (typical open-source models from Hugging Face). Dimension override supported for text-embedding-3-small/large but not for ada-002.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: For keyword search: custom bucket-sorting algorithm organizing documents into progressively smaller buckets based on ranking rules (words, typo, proximity, attribute, sort, exactness). For vector search: originally Arroy (Approximate Nearest Neighbors Oh Yeah) — a Rust port of Spotify's Annoy library using random projection trees with LMDB-backed storage. Evolving to Hannoy, a DiskANN-inspired HNSW implementation with LMDB-backed storage, combining graph-based ANN with zero-copy semantics, SIMD acceleration, and online updates. Supports cosine, Euclidean, Manhattan, and dot product distance metrics. Quantization support available.
technical_architecture.scalability: Originally limited to single-node deployments. v1.13 introduced federated search across remote instances as sharding groundwork. January 2026 update allows dynamic shard addition for horizontal scaling without architecture redesign. Enterprise Cloud supports auto-scaling and 99.999% uptime SLA. Not yet at the scale of Elasticsearch or Milvus for billions of vectors, but suitable for datasets up to tens of millions of documents per instance.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Self-hosted via precompiled binaries (Linux, macOS, Windows), Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes. Meilisearch Cloud (fully managed, AWS-based with Graviton exploration). Available on AWS Marketplace. 14-day free trial for Cloud. Enterprise Edition adds sharding, SSO/SAML, and advanced monitoring.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Hybrid search combining keyword relevance (bucket-sorting algorithm with typo tolerance, proximity, and exactness rules) and semantic vector search (via configured embedders). Score fusion combines keyword and semantic scores using affine transformation to normalize BM25-like scores against cosine similarity scores. Users can configure the semantic ratio to weight keyword vs semantic results. Federated search across multiple indexes with v1.13+. Supports dense vector search only (no native sparse vector / SPLADE support — keyword search uses its own relevance engine, not BM25 in the traditional sense).
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Meilisearch is a retrieval engine and does not provide built-in document chunking. Chunking must be done upstream before indexing. Compatible with LangChain and LlamaIndex chunking strategies (fixed-size, recursive, semantic, document-structure-aware). Users typically chunk documents externally and index them as individual Meilisearch documents.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: No built-in cross-encoder or ColBERT reranking. Meilisearch uses its own multi-criteria ranking rules system (words, typo, proximity, attribute, sort, exactness) that acts as a sophisticated relevance pipeline. For hybrid search, score fusion combines keyword and semantic scores. External reranking can be implemented via LangChain or LlamaIndex pipelines using Meilisearch as the retrieval component.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: v1.16 (October 2025) introduced multimodal embeddings for image search. Supports base64 image input, CLIP and similar multimodal embedding models, text-to-image queries, and image-to-image queries. Users can use CLIP, LLaVA, or ResNet models for visual embeddings. Meilisearch handles embedding, indexing, and search natively for multimodal content.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native knowledge graph or GraphRAG support. Meilisearch focuses on document-level search and retrieval. Can be used alongside graph databases like Neo4j in a combined architecture.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: No built-in citation or grounding verification. Documents retain their full payload (custom fields/attributes) which can include source URLs, page numbers, and metadata for downstream citation generation by the LLM layer.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: No built-in context window management. Meilisearch provides fast, relevant retrieval; context selection and compression are handled by the orchestration framework (LangChain, LlamaIndex). The /chat endpoint (January 2026) turns a Meilisearch index into a conversational AI interface, handling some retrieval-to-response optimization internally.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Sub-50ms search response times consistently reported with minimal configuration. Meilisearch prioritizes instant-feeling search experiences. Exact p99 latencies not published in standard benchmarks, but the engine is designed for real-time, typo-tolerant search where perceived speed is a core feature. Meilisearch Cloud now offers latency monitoring metrics.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Indexing performance is approximately 7x faster than Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, and Typesense. Query throughput numbers not formally published in standardized benchmarks. Meilisearch Cloud monitoring now tracks max search queries per second. The engine is optimized for search-heavy read workloads typical of e-commerce and content discovery.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: No published MTEB or BEIR scores (Meilisearch is a search engine, not an embedding model). Hybrid search accuracy depends on the configured embedder model. Keyword search accuracy benefits from built-in typo tolerance, prefix matching, and multi-criteria ranking. Case studies report 43% improvement in purchase conversion compared to previous search engines for e-commerce use cases.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Meilisearch displays strong performance for prefix and typo queries compared to competitors. Indexing speed is ~7x faster than Elasticsearch. Not typically included in ANN-Benchmarks as it is a full search engine rather than a pure vector database. Hannoy (new HNSW implementation) claims 10x speedup over the previous Arroy tree-based approach for vector search specifically. [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: LangChain (official Meilisearch vector store integration), LlamaIndex (documented RAG tutorial with Meilisearch as retrieval backend), compatible with Haystack and other orchestration frameworks via REST API. Meilisearch provides a standard RESTful HTTP API that any framework can consume. Official SDKs for 10+ languages simplify integration.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Native embedder integrations: OpenAI (text-embedding-ada-002, text-embedding-3-small, text-embedding-3-large), Hugging Face (any sentence-transformers model), Ollama (local open-source models). Any model exposable via REST endpoint can be used as a custom embedder. Users can also supply pre-computed embeddings directly, enabling use of any embedding model (Cohere, Mistral, Voyage AI, Google, etc.).
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Official MCP server available: meilisearch/meilisearch-mcp on GitHub and PyPI (pip install meilisearch-mcp). Also available via Docker (getmeili/meilisearch-mcp). Supports Claude Desktop and other MCP-compatible clients. Features include search, index management, document operations, settings management, API key management, task management, and system monitoring via natural language.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: No native first-party data connectors (unlike Elasticsearch). Data ingestion is done via the REST API or SDKs by pushing JSON documents. Third-party integration via Airbyte (300+ source connectors to Meilisearch destination), CloudQuery (Confluence, databases, etc.), and Precog. For RAG pipelines, document loaders from LangChain/LlamaIndex handle PDF, CSV, TXT, Google Drive, Confluence, Notion, Slack, and web crawl sources before indexing into Meilisearch.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Meilisearch Cloud provides built-in monitoring metrics (search performance, latency, QPS) in beta. New Relic integration available for monitoring Meilisearch instances. No native OpenTelemetry or LangSmith/Langfuse integration. When used via LangChain/LlamaIndex, tracing is handled by those frameworks' observability integrations (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix).

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core model: fully open-source MIT-licensed engine is free for self-hosting with all core features (including AI-powered search). Meilisearch Cloud offers usage-based pricing (flexible, pay-for-what-you-use) and resource-based pricing (dedicated infrastructure, predictable costs). Enterprise pricing is custom with SLA.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Self-hosted: completely free with no limits (MIT license). Meilisearch Cloud: 14-day free trial (no credit card required). No permanent free cloud tier.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Cloud Build plan: $30/month for 100,000 documents and 50,000 searches. Cloud Pro plan: $300/month for 1,000,000 documents and 250,000 searches with priority support. Resource-based pricing available for dedicated infrastructure. Self-hosted: only infrastructure costs (a small VM at ~$20-50/month can handle millions of documents). Enterprise: custom pricing for sharding, SSO, and SLA requirements.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Self-hosted: free software + infrastructure ($20-100/month for a single instance handling up to ~10M documents). Cloud managed: $30-300/month for typical startup workloads. Embedding costs are separate: OpenAI embeddings ~$0.02-0.13 per 1M tokens; Hugging Face/Ollama embedders can run locally for free. Main TCO advantage vs Algolia: dramatically lower cost at scale (Algolia can cost thousands per month for similar usage). Main TCO advantage vs Elasticsearch: simpler operations, no cluster management expertise needed.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Strong open-source challenger in the search engine market, positioned between developer-friendly simplicity (vs Elasticsearch complexity) and enterprise capabilities (vs Algolia cost). Leading in the open-source search-as-a-service category alongside Typesense. Emerging player in the RAG/AI retrieval space since v1.6 (vector search) through v1.13+ (stable AI search). Not a pure vector database competitor to Pinecone/Qdrant, but a full search engine with vector capabilities.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Louis Vuitton (global customer experience search), Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (Turkey, government, 12,734 employees), Hopper Motor Group (Australia), Esmark (Denmark), Bendigo Toyota (Australia), MotionElements (stock media marketplace). E-commerce case studies show 43% improvement in purchase conversion. Used by many developer-facing products and documentation sites.
adoption_and_market.community_size: ~48,000-56,000 GitHub stars (one of the most-starred Rust projects and search engines on GitHub), active Discord community (migrated from Slack), 200+ GitHub contributors, SDKs in 10+ languages. Docker Hub image widely pulled. Strapi plugin has 4,000+ weekly npm downloads.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: ~$20M across 3 rounds. Seed: ~$5M. Series A: $15M (October 2022, led by Felicis with participation from CRV, LocalGlobe, ESOP, Mango Capital, Seedcamp, and Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch). No additional funding rounds announced since October 2022 as of February 2026. Valuation not publicly disclosed.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Algolia (proprietary, fully managed, most mature enterprise features, but expensive), Typesense (C++ open-source, GPLv3, also fast and developer-friendly), Elasticsearch (Java, most features and scale, but complex to operate). As a vector/RAG retrieval engine: competes with Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus for the RAG retrieval layer, though Meilisearch is a full search engine, not a pure vector DB. Key differentiators: MIT license (most permissive), Rust performance, sub-50ms out-of-the-box, built-in typo tolerance, easiest setup in category, native hybrid search without requiring a separate vector DB.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Excellent fit for startups that need both traditional search (e-commerce, content discovery, documentation) AND semantic/AI search in one system. Best for: teams of 1-20 engineers who want fast setup without search infrastructure expertise, e-commerce startups needing typo-tolerant product search with semantic understanding, SaaS products adding search or AI features. Budget: free self-hosted, $30-300/month on Cloud. The MIT license means zero vendor lock-in risk. Particularly strong for French/EU startups given the company is Paris-based. Not the best choice for pure vector similarity at billion-scale (use Qdrant/Milvus) or for complex analytics (use Elasticsearch).
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Self-host when: you need full control, data sovereignty, or want to minimize costs at scale. A single developer can set up and maintain Meilisearch in production. Use Meilisearch Cloud when: team is small (<5 engineers), time-to-market is critical, or you need managed infrastructure with monitoring. Enterprise Edition when: sharding, SSO/SAML, or SLA requirements exist. Key advantage over Algolia: self-hosting is a viable, fully-featured option. Key advantage over Elasticsearch: no cluster management expertise needed.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 30 minutes to 1 day (Docker + SDK + a few API calls). MVP with search: 1-3 days. MVP with hybrid search (keyword + semantic): 3-7 days (includes embedder configuration). Full production deployment (self-hosted): 1-2 weeks including monitoring, backups, and performance tuning. Full production on Meilisearch Cloud: 2-5 days. Meilisearch is widely regarded as having the fastest time-to-production of any search engine.
key_lessons: 1. Use Meilisearch as a unified search + RAG retrieval layer — instead of running a search engine AND a vector database separately, Meilisearch's native hybrid search handles both keyword and semantic retrieval in one system, reducing infrastructure complexity and cost.

2. Start with keyword search, add AI incrementally — Meilisearch's traditional search works out of the box in minutes. Add vector embeddings later when you need semantic understanding, without changing your architecture.

3. MIT license eliminates vendor lock-in anxiety — unlike Algolia (proprietary) or Typesense (GPLv3), Meilisearch's MIT license means you can fork, modify, and embed it freely. This is a strategic advantage for startups building products on top of search.

4. Don't confuse search engines with vector databases — Meilisearch excels at user-facing search (typo tolerance, instant results, filtering) with added vector capabilities. For pure vector similarity at massive scale or complex multi-vector retrieval, purpose-built vector databases may be more appropriate.

5. Leverage the /chat endpoint for instant AI features — the January 2026 /chat endpoint turns any Meilisearch index into a conversational AI interface, enabling chatbot-style product discovery or documentation Q&A with minimal development effort.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Meilisearch includes a built-in mini-dashboard web UI for index management, document browsing, and search testing. Meilisearch Cloud provides a management console with monitoring metrics. Not a full no-code RAG pipeline builder, but the RESTful API and /chat endpoint enable low-code integrations. MCP server enables natural language interaction for AI agents.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & no-code tools — using Meilisearch's /chat and hybrid search for RAG demos) and Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy decision for search infrastructure, CRISP-DM data preparation with search indexing)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official Meilisearch documentation, blog posts, GitHub repository, TechCrunch funding reports, Crunchbase, and technical blog posts by core developer Kerollmops. Product features verified across multiple official sources.
confidence.cross_reference: Funding confirmed by TechCrunch ($15M Series A, October 2022) and Crunchbase (~$20M total). Technical architecture confirmed by Arroy and Hannoy GitHub repositories and developer blog posts. Pricing confirmed by official pricing page. Customer references from official customers page.
confidence.caveats: GitHub star count varies across sources (some say 40K+, others 50K+, one says 55.8K) — likely reflects rapid growth and different snapshot dates. No new funding since October 2022 (over 3 years), which may indicate either bootstrap/revenue sustainability or potential challenges. Vector search was experimental until v1.13 (2025) — the AI search features are relatively new compared to the mature keyword search. Horizontal scaling (sharding) is only available in Enterprise Edition, limiting the open-source version to single-node deployments. Benchmark comparisons are mostly self-published by Meilisearch; independent third-party benchmarks for vector search specifically are scarce.
confidence.security_posture: Meilisearch Cloud: SOC 2 compliance, end-to-end encryption, 99.999% uptime SLA (Enterprise). API key-based authentication with master key and search-only keys. Tenant tokens (JWT-based) for multi-tenancy with document-level access control — tokens are short-lived and not stored server-side. Enterprise Identity and Access features support SSO/SAML via IdP integration. Self-hosted: users responsible for network security, TLS termination, and access control. No specific mitigations documented for vector-specific attacks (embedding inversion, knowledge base poisoning), though standard API security practices apply.
